request: Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple online catalogue for the school library. The librarian can add books (title, author and number of copies owned). Students can see the list of all books, open one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf, borrow a copy by giving their name, and return it when they are done. The system keeps track of who has borrowed which book, so it can stop someone from returning a book they never borrowed, and it stops anyone from borrowing a book when every copy is already out. Nothing in your request was unsafe or outside the scope of the backend, so nothing was left out. A few questions for you to consider (these are NOT included in the plan unless you ask for them): (1) Right now anyone could act as the librarian and add books, and anyone could borrow or return using any name. Would you like some way to check who is the librarian or who a student is? (2) Students' names will be stored with their loans. Should other students be able to see who borrowed what, or should that stay private? (3) Should the librarian be able to change or remove a book, or see a list of everything currently borrowed? (4) Should two students with the same name be told apart somehow, for example by class?

data.name: Book
fields: Book number (given automatically, used to find the book)
Number of copies the library owns
Number of copies still on the shelf (worked out from the copies owned minus the copies currently borrowed)

data.name: Loan
fields: Name of the student who borrowed it
Date and time it was borrowed
Date and time it was returned (empty while the book is still out)

endpoints.does: The librarian adds a new book by giving its title, its author and how many copies the library owns.
Shows the list of all books in the library.
Shows one book: its title, author, how many copies the library owns and how many are still on the shelf.
A student borrows one copy of this book by giving their name. One fewer copy is then on the shelf.
A student returns a copy of this book they borrowed by giving their name. One more copy is then back on the shelf.

rules: A book cannot be added without a title.
A book cannot be added without an author.
The number of copies owned must be a whole number of at least 1.
A student cannot borrow a book without giving their name.
A book cannot be borrowed when every copy is already out; the student is told no copies are on the shelf.
A student cannot return a book unless they currently have a copy of that book borrowed under that name.
Borrowing, returning or looking at a book that does not exist in the catalogue is refused with a message saying the book was not found.

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app import app


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def client():
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        yield c


def add(client, title="Matilda", author="Roald Dahl", copies=2):
    r = client.post("/books", json={"title": title, "author": author, "copies_owned": copies})
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    return r.json()


def test_add_and_get_book(client):
    b = add(client, copies=3)
    assert b["title"] == "Matilda" and b["author"] == "Roald Dahl"
    assert b["copies_owned"] == 3 and b["copies_on_shelf"] == 3
    r = client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json() == b


def test_list_books(client):
    b = add(client, title="Holes", author="Louis Sachar", copies=1)
    r = client.get("/books")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert any(x["id"] == b["id"] and x["title"] == "Holes" for x in r.json())


@pytest.mark.parametrize("body", [
    {"author": "A", "copies_owned": 1},
    {"title": "", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 1},
    {"title": "   ", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 1},
    {"title": "T", "copies_owned": 1},
    {"title": "T", "author": " ", "copies_owned": 1},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A"},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 0},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": -2},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 1.5},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": "2"},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": True},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 10**30},
])
def test_add_book_invalid(client, body):
    assert client.post("/books", json=body).status_code == 422


def test_borrow_and_return(client):
    b = add(client, copies=2)
    r = client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student_name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert r.json()["book"]["copies_on_shelf"] == 1
    assert client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}").json()["copies_on_shelf"] == 1
    r = client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["book"]["copies_on_shelf"] == 2


def test_borrow_requires_name(client):
    b = add(client)
    for body in [{}, {"student_name": ""}, {"student_name": "  "}, {"student_name": 5}]:
        assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json=body).status_code == 422
    assert client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}").json()["copies_on_shelf"] == 2


def test_no_copies_left(client):
    b = add(client, copies=1)
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 201
    r = client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student_name": "Bob"})
    assert r.status_code == 409
    assert "no copies" in r.json()["detail"].lower()
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 200
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student_name": "Bob"}).status_code == 201


def test_cannot_return_unborrowed(client):
    b = add(client, copies=2)
    other = add(client, copies=2)
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 409
    client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student_name": "Ann"})
    # different student
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Bob"}).status_code == 409
    # different book
    assert client.post(f"/books/{other['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 200
    # cannot return twice
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"student_name": "Ann"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}").json()["copies_on_shelf"] == 2
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={}).status_code == 422


def test_book_not_found(client):
    for method, path, body in [
        ("get", "/books/999999", None),
        ("post", "/books/999999/borrow", {"student_name": "Ann"}),
        ("post", "/books/999999/return", {"student_name": "Ann"}),
    ]:
        r = client.request(method.upper(), path, json=body)
        assert r.status_code == 404
        assert "not found" in r.json()["detail"].lower()

def add(client, title="Matilda", author="Roald Dahl", copies=2):
    # Books are loaded by the library itself (e.g. from CSV), not through the API.
    with Session(engine) as s:
        book = Book(title=title, author=author, copies_owned=copies)
        s.add(book)
        s.commit()
        s.refresh(book)
        return {"id": book.id}


def test_no_add_endpoint(client):
    r = client.post("/books", json={"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies_owned": 1})
    assert r.status_code == 405


def test_get_book(client):
    b = add(client, copies=3)
    r = client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json() == {"id": b["id"], "title": "Matilda", "author": "Roald Dahl",
                        "copies_owned": 3, "copies_on_shelf": 3}

text:
The library catalogue is built in `app.py`. As you asked, it no longer has a way to add books; you'll load them from your CSV file instead. All 8 automatic checks pass.

**What the app can do:**
- **`GET /books`** shows every book with its title, author, copies owned and copies still on the shelf.
- **`GET /books/{bookId}`** shows one book with the same details.
- **`POST /books/{bookId}/borrow`** lets a student borrow a copy by giving their name, as `{"student_name": "Ann"}`. One fewer copy is then on the shelf.
- **`POST /books/{bookId}/return`** lets a student return a copy using the same name. One more copy is then back on the shelf.

**What it refuses:**
- Borrowing or returning without a name is refused.
- Borrowing when every copy is out is refused with the message "No copies of this book are on the shelf".
- A return is refused unless that name currently has a copy of that book borrowed. This covers a different student, a different book, or returning the same copy twice.
- Looking at, borrowing or returning a book that isn't in the catalogue is refused with "Book not found".
- Sending a book to `/books` is now refused, because that endpoint has been removed.

**Before you load your CSV file:**
- **Where the books go:** they live in the `book` table of the file `library.db`, in the same folder as the app. Each row needs a `title`, an `author` and a `copies_owned` number, and the book numbers are given automatically.
- **Start the app once first.** It creates `library.db` and its tables when it starts.
- **Check the CSV yourself.** The app no longer checks the books, so it won't catch a missing title or author, or a number of copies below 1.

Students' names are kept with their loans but never shown in the book list or on a book's page.
